notes: NCI PDQ was reread for Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor as an ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor that may secrete androgens and present with virilization or secondary amenorrhea.
NCI Dictionary independently confirms testosterone production and virilizing physical changes.
Peer-reviewed pathology material was checked for Sertoli-cell tubules/cords with clusters of Leydig cells, directly supporting the microscopic key.
Official USMLE Content Outline (2026) female reproductive section includes ovarian neoplasms.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.virilization_pattern: Rapid virilization and markedly elevated testosterone are compatible with androgen secretion by Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor.
claim_audit.DHEAS_localization: Normal DHEA-S makes a major adrenal androgen source less likely and supports ovarian localization when an ovarian mass is present; it is used as a clue, not an absolute exclusion rule.
claim_audit.key_histology: Typical Sertoli-Leydig morphology includes Sertoli-type tubules/cords with Leydig-cell clusters.
claim_audit.granulosa_distractor: Call-Exner bodies and grooved nuclei identify granulosa-cell differentiation, not the virilizing Sertoli-Leydig pattern.
claim_audit.dysgerminoma_distractor: Dysgerminoma shows large clear cells with fibrous septa and lymphocytes and is a germ-cell tumor.
claim_audit.serous_distractor: Papillae with psammoma bodies correspond to serous differentiation.
claim_audit.teratoma_distractor: Mature tissues from multiple germ layers indicate mature teratoma.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Without the staged key, the combination of rapid virilization, high testosterone, normal DHEA-S, and a unilateral ovarian mass points to an androgen-producing ovarian sex cord-stromal tumor. Among the microscopic options, Sertoli-type tubules with Leydig cells is uniquely congruent.
adversarial_second_pass.granulosa_attack: Both granulosa and Sertoli-Leydig tumors are sex cord-stromal, but granulosa tumors are classically estrogenic and the listed Call-Exner morphology does not match the androgenic syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.adrenal_attack: The vignette does not claim normal DHEA-S absolutely excludes adrenal disease; the actual ovarian mass plus testosterone-predominant virilization establishes the intended localization.
adversarial_second_pass.dicer1_precision_check: DICER1 is mentioned only as an association in the explanation/mechanism and is not required for diagnosis or asserted to be universal.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five answers are microscopic patterns of genuine ovarian tumors at similar descriptive depth.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No tumor-grade assumption, mutation frequency, testosterone threshold, age cutoff, or management claim is required.
